text:
alex: Heads-up — CUST-12 is seeing p99 latency spikes for inference requests from EU users to models hosted in APAC. p95 moved a bit, but p99 jumped ~380ms starting ~06:30 UTC. Opening thread for triage. attaching quick probe outputs.

sam: I see the spike on the regional latency dashboard. It correlates with a route change where some EU egresses started traversing an extra hop toward ap-southeast before hitting the model pool. possible geo-path skew.

lina: Can you paste the traceroute you ran from the EU probe?

alex: sure, pasted below (trimmed):
```
traceroute to model-v2.redwood.example (203.0.113.101), 10 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.1.0.1 (10.1.0.1)  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.1 ms
 2  198.51.100.10 (198.51.100.10)  12.3 ms  12.1 ms  12.0 ms
 3  198.51.100.45 (198.51.100.45)  14.5 ms  14.4 ms  14.3 ms
 4  203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45)  42.1 ms  42.0 ms  41.9 ms  <-- apac-edge
 5  198.51.100.22 (198.51.100.22)  412.8 ms  413.0 ms  412.9 ms  <-- back to eu-pop??
 6  203.0.113.101 (203.0.113.101)  425.2 ms  425.1 ms  425.3 ms
```

morton: interesting — looks like some traffic is getting detoured across APAC then back to EU, creating a long RTT tail. That explains the p99 tail. Could be an anycast shard shift or stale DNS resolver cached route.

support-bot: ALERT: p99 > 350ms for model-v2 serving region=eu-west customers=CUST-12 count=118/min at 06:38 UTC

sam: let's validate DNS answers from affected resolvers and our authoritative. can you run: `dig +short @8.8.8.8 model-v2.redwood.example` and also `dig +trace model-v2.redwood.example` from the probe host?

alex: ran dig from probe:
```
# dig +short @8.8.8.8 model-v2.redwood.example
203.0.113.101
203.0.113.102
# dig +trace model-v2.redwood.example
.  518400 IN NS a.root-servers.net.
... (truncated)
model-v2.redwood.example. 3600 IN A 203.0.113.101
model-v2.redwood.example. 3600 IN A 203.0.113.102
```

lina: TTL is 3600s on the authoritative record — that could lock resolvers into stale anycast mapping for longer than we want. Some long-lived resolvers in customers' networks appear to have a path that briefly preferred the apac-edge prefix.

sam: also check TLS handshake durations — if connections are establishing fresh handshakes instead of resuming, that adds big tail. run tcpdump and measure handshake timing for SYN -> TLS Finished.

alex: collecting pcap now: `tcpdump -i eth0 host 203.0.113.101 and port 443 -w /tmp/eu_apac.pcap` — watching for TLS "ServerHello" delays. From a small sample i see handshake time ~360-420ms on affected flows. many are full TLS handshakes, session tickets not used consistently.

morton: probable root: resolver picks apac-pop IP due to anycast shard inconsistency at some upstream; connections then bounce back due to BGP or proxying, causing cross-region detour + full TLS handshakes. Two orthogonal mitigations: reduce DNS TTL to force re-resolve to closer anycast shard, and enable TLS session tickets/resumption to avoid repeated full handshakes.

sam: short-term mitigation plan: 1) apply per-customer routing preference to pin CUST-12 to eu-pop IP prefixes, 2) lower authoritative A record TTL to 30s, 3) enable session ticket resume on serving pool for model-v2 if not already. We need quick canary.

alex: I'll push the routing preference flag to CUST-12 first (canary to 5% of their traffic) and monitor p99 for 10m. command i'll run: 
```
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/route/flags" \
  -d '{"flag":"route.strict_region_preference","value":true,"customers":["CUST-12"],"percent":5}'
```

deploy-bot: route flag rollout started for CUST-12 at 07:02 UTC (5%)

alex: monitoring metrics... sending tcpdump to S3 link: https://s3.internal/redwood/triage/eu_apac/4623456789.pcap

(5m pass)

sam: early signal looks promising — p99 dropped from ~420ms to ~95ms on the canary traffic. nice.

lina: if canary stays good, do global customer pin for CUST-12 and roll TTL change. We should also open a follow-up to evaluate our anycast shard convergence — maybe some POP had an unhealthy node and the health-check routing rebalanced incorrectly.

morton: notes for postmortem: - root: temporary anycast routing drift + long DNS TTL - contributing: TLS full-handshake exposure - mitigation taken: per-customer route pin, lowered TTL, enabled session resumption - long-term: add active resolver health checks, reduce cross-region failover aggressiveness, harmonize TTLs to <60s for critical endpoints.

alex: applied full-customer routing pin at 07:12 UTC and lowered TTL to 30s. Also toggled session ticket resume on pool-variant v2-rc1.

deploy-bot: policy applied: route.strict_region_preference=true for customer=CUST-12 at 07:12 UTC

support-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: p99 for model-v2 customers=CUST-12 returned to baseline (p99 ~90ms) at 07:18 UTC

sam: rolling back nothing — keep mitigations for now while we investigate the anycast convergence. I'll open a tracking ticket and ping net-eng.

alex: created ticket RED-5402 with details + pcap + traceroute. will draft short postmortem. thanks all. :thumbsup:

lina: quick action items — I'll own follow-up with net-eng on anycast convergence, morton please draft remediation doc for TTL policy, sam please coordinate with product to standardize session-resume defaults.

morton: on it.

sam: thanks everyone. marking thread resolved for now.
